sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: DOMINANT UPPER-AIR FEATURE REMAINS STG RIDGING FROM CA-CAROLINAS...WITH 500-MB HIGH OVER 4-CORNERS REGION. STG SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE EWD ACROSS FAR NRN ONT TOWARD SRN HUDSON/JAMES BAYS...WITH SRN FRINGE OF HEIGHT FALLS BRUSHING LOWER MI/LH REGION. HEIGHTS WILL FALL OVER PAC NW WITH APCH OF TROUGH THAT EXTENDS SEWD FROM MID-UPPER CYCLONE OVER ERN GULF OF AK. SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS EVIDENT IN MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY OVER SERN MT AND ERN WY...INVOF ONGOING CONVECTION THERE...AND TRACING BACK AT LEAST TO 24 HOURS AGO OVER SRN ORE. THIS FEATURE IS FCST TO MOVE ENEWD ACROSS WRN DAKOTAS...REACHING TO NEAR MO RIVER IN SD/ND BY END OF PERIOD. AT SFC...COLD FRONT WAS ANALYZED FROM CENTRAL LOWER MI SWWD ACROSS CENTRAL IL TO CENTRAL MO...BECOMING QUASISTATIONARY WWD OVER CENTRAL KS TO E-CENTRAL CO. ERN PORTION OF FRONT SHOULD REACH WRN NY...NWRN PA...SRN OH...AND SRN INDIANA BY END OF PERIOD...PERHAPS OBSCURED BY ANTECEDENT MCS OUTFLOWS.

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN HIGH PLAINS TO CENTRAL KS
sections.text: SCATTERED TO WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS FROM SERN MT TO ERN WY AND NEB PANHANDLE. OCNL SUPERCELL EVOLUTION STILL IS POSSIBLE IN RELATIVELY DISCRETE CELLS...AMIDST 35-45 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES...ALTHOUGH MODES WILL BECOME MORE COMPLEX/MULTICELLULAR WITH TIME AS OUTFLOW SPREADS AWAY FROM EXISTING CONVECTION. FARTHER S...QUASISTATIONARY OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM EARLIER NEB CONVECTION IS ANALYZED N OF FRONT...FROM SERN NEB WSWWD ACROSS NRN KS NEAR HLC...THEN WNWWD INTO CONVECTION NEAR AKO. TWO PRIMARY COMPLEXES OF SCATTERED-NUMEROUS TSTMS OVER ERN CO MAY DEVELOP AGGREGATE COLD POOL AND EVOLVE INTO FORWARD-PROPAGATING MCS WITH PRIMARY WIND THREAT AS FAR E AS CENTRAL KS OVERNIGHT...FOCUSING INVOF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND FRONTAL ZONE WHERE LOW-LEVEL LIFT WILL BE RELATIVELY MAXIMIZED AHEAD OF COLD POOL. 59 KT GUST AT LIC AND 52 KT GUST AT AKO HAVE OCCURRED WITH THIS ACTIVITY. ADDITIONAL STG-SVR GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE AS DOWNDRAFTS PENETRATE RELATIVELY HOT/WELL-MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER AIR S OF BOUNDARY AND NEAR WRN SEGMENT OF FRONTAL ZONE...AND COLD POOL MOVES ESEWD-SEWD. OTHERWISE...REF SPC WWS 585-586 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST NEAR-TERM FCST GUIDANCE.

sections.title: ERN MO TO LH/LE
sections.text: A COUPLE OF BANDS OF STG-SVR TSTMS ARE EVIDENT AHEAD OF COLD FRONT FROM ERN IL ENEWD ACROSS SRN LOWER MI INTO SRN ONT...WITH POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING GUSTS AND OCNL LARGE HAIL AS THEY MOVE INTO HIGH-THETAE AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY SFC TEMPS 90S F AND DEW POINTS 70S F ON AMERICAN SIDE. WIND THREAT MAY PERSIST ACROSS LE AND OVER PORTIONS NERN OH/WRN PA/WRN NY WITH ERN COMPLEX AS WELL. REF WWS 583-584 AND ACCOMPANYING MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST NEAR-TERM FCST INFORMATION ON THIS CORRIDOR.

sections.title: CENTRAL MO TO CENTRAL KS
sections.text: MORE ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE FARTHER WSW ACROSS MO/KS INVOF SFC FRONT...WITH PROGRESSIVELY WEAKER FRONTAL CONVERGENCE AND DEEP-LAYER SHEAR LIMITING COVERAGE/ORGANIZATION. STILL..MLCAPE 3500-4500 J/KG ACROSS MO AND DEEP/WELL-MIXED SUBCLOUD LAYERS ALONG/S OF FRONT OVER KS MAY SUPPORT POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING DOWNDRAFTS AND ISOLATED HAIL WITH MOST INTENSE TSTMS. ..EDWARDS.. 07/03/2011
